plan.topic: Tirzepatide vs Foundayo (orforglipron): has the weekly shot ever been tested head to head against the daily pill?
plan.angle: Tirzepatide vs the Foundayo (orforglipron) pill: no randomized trial has compared them head to head. Two separate 72-week trials in adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes report averages: SURMOUNT-1 for tirzepatide and ATTAIN-1 for orforglipron. Give each top-dose average vs placebo using the same estimand, with an on-screen caveat: 'separate trials, different designs, not a head-to-head'. How each is taken, from label wording: a once-weekly injection vs a once-daily tablet taken with or without food. Both list nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting as common. Close with: 'A bigger average isn't best for everyone. The right choice depends on you and your prescriber.' Then the don't-switch line, the Exp F line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line.

plan.why: 'Pill vs shot' questions are rising after the China approval and US prescription records, 'foundayo' is our top non-EloraTZP search term, and tirzepatide-first comparison Shorts in obesity get 108–177 views. | fact-check: The core claim is confirmed: no randomized head-to-head of orforglipron vs tirzepatide has been reported. Orforglipron's published head-to-head was against oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes. That makes a 'what's confirmed?' Short reasonable. Risks: (a) Cross-trial numbers invite ranking. Both figures must use the same estimand. ATTAIN-1's headline and SURMOUNT-1's 20.9% may use different estimands, so take both from the same analysis (treatment-regimen in both, or efficacy in both). If they can't be matched, use none. (b) 'No food or water rules' goes beyond the label. The label says 'with or without food'. The water claim comes from press and trial descriptions, not label wording. (c) Give the highest-dose arm of each only with 'separate trials, different designs, not head-to-head' on screen in the same card. Don't use a split-screen 'winner' visual. (d) ATTAIN-1 is orforglipron's own approved-obesity data, so the title is fine. It's tirzepatide-first, as the playbook requires.

package.title: Tirzepatide vs Foundayo: Ever Tested Head to Head? #shorts
package.description:
No published trial has tested tirzepatide head to head against Foundayo (orforglipron). Two separate 72-week trials in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related health problem, and no diabetes: tirzepatide's top dose averaged 20.9% weight loss vs 3.1% on placebo; orforglipron's top trial dose averaged 11.2% vs 2.1% on placebo. Separate trials, different designs, not head-to-head.

Common on both labels: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting. Don't switch medicines on your own.

Sources:
SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35658024/
ATTAIN-1, NEJM 2025: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40960239/
Zepbound Prescribing Information (revised 8/2026): https://uspl.lilly.com/zepbound/zepbound.html
Foundayo Prescribing Information (revised 7/2026): https://uspl.lilly.com/foundayo/foundayo.html

#Tirzepatide #Orforglipron #GLP1

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Tirzepatide's top dose averaged 20.9% weight loss versus 3.1% on placebo. Orforglipron's top trial dose averaged 11.2% versus 2.1% on placebo. Same type of analysis, but different trials, different designs, not a direct comparison.

Both labels list nausea, diarrhea and vomiting among the common side effects. A bigger number on paper isn't automatically the better choice for your body. That's a conversation for you and your prescriber.

factcheck.summary:
The claims hold up. As far as I could find, no head-to-head trial of tirzepatide vs orforglipron has been published. The only head-to-head result I found for orforglipron is against oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes (ACHIEVE-3). The switching/maintenance studies aren't direct comparisons. The numbers check out:
- ATTAIN-1 (NEJM, Sept 2025): 3,127 adults without diabetes, 72 weeks, primary result by treatment-regimen estimand. Orforglipron 36 mg averaged −11.2% vs placebo −2.1%.
- SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM, 2022): tirzepatide 15 mg averaged −20.9% vs placebo −3.1% at 72 weeks, also by treatment-regimen estimand. So "same analysis type" is accurate.
- Foundayo label (revised 7/2026): once-daily tablet, taken with or without food. Nausea, diarrhea and vomiting are among its common (≥5%) adverse reactions.
- Zepbound label (revised 8/2026): once-weekly injection, with the same three listed as common.

The framing is careful. The caveat ("separate trials, different designs, not head-to-head") sits in the same scene as the second number, nothing ranks one drug above the other, and the safety lines are present. The PubMed pages wouldn't load for me because they need cookies. The ATTAIN-1 PubMed record was confirmed through search; the SURMOUNT-1 PMID was checked from memory, not loaded. Three minor fixes are listed below: scope and dose clarity, and the order of the closing lines. Not one of them is a reason to hold.

issues.claim: Orforglipron top trial dose avg, ATTAIN-1; placebo −2.1%
issues.problem: The trial dose (36 mg) is labelled differently from the marketed dose. On the Foundayo label the top dose is 17.2 mg, and the label's Trial 1 table reports −11.1%, not −11.2%. A viewer might think the strength printed on the Foundayo label is not what was tested. The narration's 'trial's top dose' is accurate; this fix just makes the on-screen card clearer.
issues.fix: stat_label: "Orforglipron top trial dose (36 mg; labelled 17.2 mg on Foundayo) avg, ATTAIN-1; placebo −2.1%; 72 wks, no diabetes"

issues.claim: adults with obesity or overweight, no diabetes
issues.problem: Both trials accepted people with overweight (BMI 27 to under 30) only if they had at least one weight-related health problem. Without that, the population sounds broader than it was.
issues.fix: Narration: "We have two separate seventy-two-week trials, in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related health problem, and no diabetes." List item: "Adults with obesity, or overweight + a weight-related condition; no diabetes"

issues.claim: Exp F line placed before the disclaimer and prescriber line
issues.problem: The playbook says the Exp F subscribe line should be second to last, just before 'Full breakdown…'. The craft notes say the safety order is the don't-switch line, then 'Not personal advice', then the prescriber line. Here the prescriber line comes second to last and Exp F comes before the disclaimer. The test only stays clean if the line order is the same across Shorts.
issues.fix: S2-7 narration: "Don't switch medicines on your own. Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you." S2-8 narration: "We answer one tirzepatide question from the research every day. Subscribe if that helps. Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description." Keep the full disclaimer + prescriber text as on-screen text in S2-7, and make S2-8's on-screen text the subscribe line.
